sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Pet Supplies and Pet Care Devices

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated and amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 7 July 2022; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulations thereunder; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 (SCSp regime, Art. 101-1 et seq.)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each natural person partner and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Police or consular authority of country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Incumbency for each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registered agent in the partner's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of criminal record (casier judiciaire) for each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national criminal records office of country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization with certified translation into French or German

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and business address (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization with certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the Luxembourg incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the grantor's home jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, managers, UBOs and authorized signatories against: (i) Luxembourg and EU PEP lists (extended to foreign PEPs, family members and close associates per Art. 3 of the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02); (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list and EU Regulation 269/2014, including Luxembourg national freeze measures; (iv) OFAC SDN list on a risk-adjusted basis given USD payment rails (Stripe, PayPal). Screening is performed at onboarding and continuously during the business relationship; enhanced due diligence is applied upon any positive PEP or sanctions hit; source-of-funds documentation is required for all capital contributions exceeding EUR 10,000.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), electronic filing portal: www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The partnership deed (contrat de société) must be drafted in French, German, or Luxembourgish, with French or German prevailing for RCSL filings; the company name may be expressed in any Latin-alphabet language provided it is not misleading, does not contravene public policy, and uses a clear transliteration into Latin script for registration purposes; the RCSL registers the Latin-script version and any accented characters are normalized for electronic records.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The chosen name is pre-checked via the LBR/RCSL portal; upon successful clearance, a priority reservation is recorded for 30 days, renewable once for an additional 30-day period upon written request before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with LBR/RCSL within 15 days of the rejection notice, with no filing fee. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may: (i) appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within one month for registration-related refusals, or (ii) bring an administrative appeal before the Tribunal administratif within three months where the refusal is characterized as an administrative decision. Legal representation by a Luxembourg avocat is mandatory for judicial appeals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional: the SCSp must have a siège social fixed in Luxembourg (Art. 101-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915). A licensed domiciliation or corporate-services provider with a physical address and local representative is acceptable and common for an e-commerce retail SCSp; a pure virtual address with no physical presence, no local representative, and no access to corporate records is not permissible for RCSL registration or for opening bank, Stripe, or PayPal accounts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 5–10% per annum probability for a low-risk, unlicensed electronic retail of pet supplies; unannounced physical on-site inspections are primarily AML/UBO-driven and may be carried out by the Luxembourg police, CSSF, or the RBE registrar in the event of inconsistent UBO declarations or suspicious transaction reports.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance, priority check, and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for name reservation (approx. EUR 40)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of partnership deed or certified signatures on private deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark EUR 900–1,500 per standard SCSp deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL registration filing fee (inscription au registre de commerce)
Publication of incorporation extract in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
UBO register (RBE) declaration filing with supporting documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RBE electronic filing is free of charge; administrative agent handling at prevailing market rate EUR 30–50

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization bundle for five foreign-origin partner and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Luxembourg apostille) and embassy/consular authorities of source jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per apostille (approx. EUR 20 in Luxembourg) plus foreign consular fees, translation certification, and courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation services – first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark EUR 1,200–2,000 per annum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees: drafting partnership agreement, AML/UBO due diligence and profiling, name clearance, and incorporation coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed-fee market benchmark EUR 2,500–4,000 for a standard SCSp with low-risk e-commerce scope

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 944-1 to 944-11 (SCSp regime) as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013, together with the Luxembourg Civil Code (Book III, Title IX) on partnership contracts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de Société (Limited Partnership Agreement) registered with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; SCSp has no minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; capital and contribution terms are contractually determined in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This pro-forma resolution is adopted on [DATE] by the general partner of the SCSp acting under the partnership agreement and the Law of 10 August 1915. RESOLVED: that the partnership application and capital contribution schedule are approved; that each initial partner subscribes to the contribution set opposite the partner’s name in the capital table; that the registered office of the partnership is established at [address in Luxembourg]; and that [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant) with sole signature authority for RCS filing, banking, VAT, and tax registration formalities. The manager is authorized to execute and submit all declarations and publications required for the SCSp’s legal existence and good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – online reservation service via lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed SCSp name. Ensure the name complies with Luxembourg naming rules, is not misleading, and contains no protected elements. The reservation is valid for a limited period; proceed promptly.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filing via a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new request with a revised name or appeal the refusal to the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (if executed by notarial deed) or the contracting partners (if executed by private writing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and finalize the limited partnership agreement containing the SCSp name, registered office address, object, duration, contribution schedule, management powers of the general partner, and provisions on limited partners. Execute the agreement by all general and limited partners, either before a notary or by private deed with legalized signatures if required.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all partners
Proof of residential address for each partner
Evidence of the registered office address (lease or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary raises formal objections or a partner fails to sign, correct the drafting defect, resubmit the corrected deed, or substitute an eligible partner without delaying the filing sequence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – filed through the eJustice electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed partnership agreement, the manager acceptance declaration, and all supporting documents to the RCS. Pay the statutory filing fee and obtain the registration number. The filing is legally effective once recorded in the RCS register.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of the general partner and manager
Proof of registered office address in Luxembourg
Declaration of non-insolvency or good standing for the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rectification notice, cure the indicated deficiency, submit the amended document through eJustice, and request expedited re-examination to avoid loss of the filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RES publication service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, prepare the legal notice summarizing the SCSp’s constitution, registered office, manager, and registration number. Submit the notice to the RES to comply with Luxembourg public disclosure requirements.
required_dossiers: Full text of the legal notice in French or German
Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RES rejects or delays the notice, verify formatting and language compliance, correct the notice text, resubmit, and, if necessary, request priority publication by contacting LBR customer support.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Social Security Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT and corporate/partnership tax purposes if applicable. Enroll the manager and any employees with the CCSS workers’ registry. Submit the EORI application if customs transactions are anticipated.
required_dossiers: Bank account and VAT questionnaires as required by AED
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED or CCSS issues a deficiency notice, supply the missing documentation or amend the submitted declarations through MyGuichet.lu; late penalties may be waived upon prompt correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 4791 (electronic retailing of pet supplies) requires no industrial manufacturing permit in Luxembourg.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operating license is mandated for pure e-commerce retailing; the business must comply with the Luxembourg Consumer Code and the e-Commerce Directive.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA or registration is required for an e-commerce warehousing and distribution activity falling below the thresholds set out in the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Retail-only and warehousing activity; no manufacturing discharges; process wastewater not present. Volatile organic compound emissions are limited to negligible levels, and any waste must be collected and disposed of in accordance with the Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office/warehouse must obtain municipal fire safety certification under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 November 2009 on fire safety, and a structural soundness certificate for any occupied premises; workplace clearance must satisfy the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) rules on occupational health and safety, including first-aid and emergency evacuation provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority) for VAT matters; Administration des contributions directes (Direct Tax Administration) for income tax matters; unified business registration via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through guichet.lu / MyGuichet portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg-established SCSp, the entity must first register with the Luxembourg Business Registers to obtain the national business registration number (matricule). The SCSp must subsequently apply for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro d'identification TVA) using Form 16 filed with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA. A non-resident foreign entity making taxable supplies in Luxembourg and not established in the EU must appoint a VAT fiscal representative approved by the Luxembourg VAT administration; an EU-established foreign entity may register directly with Form 16. The application must be filed before commencing taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime. The SCSp is mandatorily treated as fiscally transparent for income and net wealth tax purposes (partners are taxed directly). No election to opt into corporate income tax is available. For VAT purposes, the SCSp is a taxable person; it may elect to form a VAT group (assujetti unique) with related Luxembourg-established entities, subject to prior AEDT approval. Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD apply to deny deductions on arrangements exploiting mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover for domestic small business exemption); mandatory VAT registration is triggered without threshold for non-established foreign suppliers and for any taxable B2C e-commerce activity when the small enterprise exemption is not claimed or is exceeded. Cross-border EU distance sales have a separate EUR 10,000 pan-EU threshold for the destination state unless the OSS scheme is used.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general real-time fiscal clearance, API-based reporting, or digital stamping mandate applies to domestic B2B/B2C invoicing in Luxembourg. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G transactions and must be submitted through PEPPOL BIS 3.0. For e-commerce supplies, standard VAT invoice rules apply; while Stripe/PayPal generate payment records, they are not substitutes for statutory VAT invoicing. Luxembourg is expected to align with EU ViDA real-time e-invoicing proposals in due course, but no such obligation is currently in force for the described pet products e-commerce activity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical pet supplies from Luxembourg to destinations outside the EU qualify for zero-rating where the supplier retains proof that the goods left the EU within the prescribed time limits (generally within 90 days of supply). The SCSp must issue a zero-rated invoice, obtain a customs export declaration, and maintain transport evidence. Services connected to supplies of pet care devices rendered to non-EU customers may be zero-rated where the customer is a taxable person established outside the EU, or where the effective use and enjoyment of B2C digital services occurs outside the EU. Sales of goods to EU consumers are not export zero-rated; they are taxable in the member state of destination via the OSS scheme or local VAT registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Export Control System / Movement Reference Number) confirming the goods left Luxembourg and the EU
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical transport of the goods outside the EU
Inward remittance certificate or bank settlement evidence showing payment from the foreign buyer in foreign currency and receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may reject export zero-rating if the documentary evidence is incomplete or untimely. Where zero-rating is unjustly applied, the tax authority issues a VAT assessment for the unpaid VAT plus default interest at an annual rate of 5%, and imposes administrative fines ranging from 10% to 20% of the disputed tax. Deliberately fraudulent claims under Articles 72–79 of the Luxembourg VAT Law expose the SCSp and its managers to criminal penalties, including fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment; retrospective clawback is not time-barred for fraudulent declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem; banking and payment supervision by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the CSSF Law and EU financial services acquis. No separate foreign-exchange administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full euro-zone currency convertibility. It applies no material distinction between current-account and capital-account transactions under the EU Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (free movement of capital) and the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial undertakings, as amended. Capital injections, operating revenues, profit remittances, and repatriation of invested capital may be denominated in EUR or freely convertible foreign currency without convertibility restrictions. Practical hurdles are administrative: compliance with CSD/BCL payment systems, AML/KYC onboarding, the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE), FATCA/CRS reporting, EU sanctions/asset freeze regulation, and, for non-resident investors, relevant inbound/outbound investment statute and tax transparency documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory EUR conversion applies. Luxembourg/EU law does not impose a timeline for repatriating export receipts, nor any conversion ratio into EUR. Export proceeds may be kept in foreign currency, netted in treasury, or converted under permitted FX contracts. For statistical and prudential purposes, the BCL compiles Balance of Payments data, and Intrastat/foreign-trade declarations and corporate accounting records must evidence the underlying transactions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Société Générale Bank & Solutions S.A., Luxembourg
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with FX Hedging Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for non-EU/offshore digital e-money institutions; Medium for EU/EEA-licensed EMIs and PSD2-authorized payment institutions that passport into Luxembourg. An offshore EMI lacking an EU/EEA licence cannot provide payment accounts, local IBANs, or direct clearing access without CSSF authorization and is legally unsuitable for capital escrow, trade settlement, or statutory regulatory buffers. For contingency liquidity and low-value e-commerce collections, only EMIs with a valid e-money licence from an EEA regulator and an active cross-border passport notification under PSD2 may be used as a complementary payment rail; they must not be the sole treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement under Luxembourg law for all partners to appear physically. In practice, tier-1 banks require at least the general partner/managing partner and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) to complete a face-to-face or supervisory-technology validated video KYC interview before account activation. Remote onboarding is possible if the bank accepts an eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic signature, digital passport verification, and an official confirmation of residence/address. The bank may require one in-person meeting in Luxembourg for corporate GP representatives signing account mandates; this can often be fulfilled via the bank’s correspondent or approved office. Documentation must include the partnership agreement, RCS registration extract, UBO register, resolutions, passport copies, proof of address, source of wealth/funds, and a written economic-substance statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SCSp is tax-transparent and unregulated, allowing multiple passive non-resident partners to sit outside a conventional corporate KYC perimeter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official RCS extract; executed partnership agreement; partner register with full name, date of birth, jurisdiction, and percentage interest; UBO register filed with the Luxembourg RBE; a legal opinion by a Luxembourg qualified lawyer confirming pass-through status and the identity of the general partner; comprehensive corporate structure chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward partner capital contributions cannot be distinguished from unrelated third-party funding or shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment records; bank reference letters; executed capital contribution or loan agreements; each partner's source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement; proof of regulatory status of the originating bank; notarized resolutions where corporate partners are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border e-commerce transaction laundering risk associated with digital-only pet supplies sales and use of PSPs such as Stripe and PayPal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full business plan and customer acquisition model; verified marketplace/seller agreements; historical sales ledger and platform payout statements; supplier contracts, invoices, and logistics providers' records; refund and chargeback policies; sanctions screening and geoblocking procedures; current chargeback ratio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore digital EMI receipts create an opaque payment chain and commingled treasury balances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete payment-services provider mapping; confirmation that all PSPs are EEA-regulated and hold client funds at licensed credit institutions; contractual flow-of-funds acknowledgements; daily reconciliation reports from the EMI or gateway; prohibition on third-party payouts to unverified beneficiary accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to sanctioned counterparties or exports of dual-use/restricted pet-care electronic devices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated global denied-party screening logs; product classification under EU dual-use Regulation 2021/821; jurisdiction-specific selling restrictions; proof of no Russian, Belarusian, Crimean, Iranian, or north-Korean nexus; end-user and end-use declarations for high-ticket electronic devices.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital injections must be wired from an actual bank account in the partner's name to the SCSp's segregated Luxembourg IBAN via SWIFT MT202 bank-to-bank transfer and accompanied by an MT103 customer credit transfer remittance advice. Use the EU Balance of Payments direct-investment purpose code for equity contributions or the appropriate code for shareholder loans, and include the SCSp's RCS number and payment reference in the narration. The bank will verify the ultimate originator, source of funds, sanctions status, and clearing path; no exchange-control approval is required. Funds should be received in the currency of the capital commitment, mapped in the treasury ledger to each partner's capital account, and only then converted or deployed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro payments to Luxembourg and EEA suppliers, use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or, for amounts outside SEPA, SWIFT MT103. For USD, CNY, and other non-EUR currencies, clear through the bank's correspondent network using MT103 with full beneficiary details, reference to the underlying invoice or purchase order, and required invoice and customs documentation. Large or recurring pet-product supply orders from Asia and the USA can be secured via a documentary Letter of Credit (UCP 600), typically an irrevocable commercial LC issued by the buying SCSp's bank and advised or confirmed by the supplier's bank; bank guarantee and cash-deposit collateral may be required. All outbound payments should be matched to the commercial contract, shipment evidence, and customs declarations, and kept free of sanctioned jurisdictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and other freely convertible currencies) for committed trade settlements and expected receipts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or low-liquidity market currencies, settled in EUR or USD against agreed reference rates
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and basis swaps) for matching longer-term partner capital balances and trade-finance cash-flow streams

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of registration details (déclaration annuelle) to the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCSL – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary of registration date in the RCSL (calendar anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filling fines from EUR 100 to EUR 1,000 per representative; two consecutive non-filings trigger an automatic striking-off procedure from the RCSL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) data in the beneficial ownership register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RBE – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (via Luxembourg Business Registers e-file platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within one month after the anniversary of the company's RCSL registration; immediate update within 15 days after any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 and criminal sanctions for managers; recurrent failure may be reported to the Public Prosecutor and lead to forced strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements filing (mandatory only if the SCSp exceeds the Luxembourg size thresholds or has the status of a holding company; otherwise exempt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCSL / Central Balance Sheet Office (Centrale des Bilans)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end; non-prorogable filing by 31 December if the financial year closes on 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing fines up to EUR 2,500; persistent failure can result in court-ordered liquidation and disqualification of managers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Luxembourg law requires a statutory audit if two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million, net turnover > EUR 8.8 million, average headcount > 50; certain SCSp structures (e.g. SIF or AIF) are always subject to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable normalisé, PCN) based on the Law of 19 December 2002; IFRS permitted for voluntary consolidated financial statements or mandatory for listed entities and credit institutions

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually confirm UBO details on the RBE portal within one month of the RCSL registration anniversary. If shareholding/data changes, file an update within 15 days of the change; UBO information must always mirror current ownership, and failure to include a legal partner entity trigger must be documented.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Members) – mandatory for SCSp
Register of Managers (General and Special Limited Partners)
Minute Book (deliberations of general partners and limited partner consents)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg headline CIT/MBS in Luxembourg City for a taxable corporate entity; transparent SCSp is not itself subject to CIT.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral tax holiday; 80% IP income exemption, participation exemption for qualifying dividends/capital gains, investment tax credits, and transparent pass-through at SCSp level; ordinary e-commerce trading profit is taxable at the partner level.
